grade_reason: In an October 2026 op-ed co-written with Sen. McCormick he says AI models can pose credible biological, cyber or nuclear risks and could cause catastrophic harm, without extinction framing. He also rejected 'AI doomsdaying' in August 2026 and opposes any pause, so the reviewer should weigh the F-level remark against the later op-ed.
notes: Seven web searches ran, all succeeded. The op-ed quotes were read in The Center Square's report (republished on Just the News), not in The Free Press itself, which is paywalled after the introduction; the op-ed date shown there is 10.01.26. The op-ed is co-authored with Sen. Dave McCormick, so the words are joint. Other op-ed wording seen in the same report but not used as separate statements: the 'existential stakes of the AI race with China' (about the race, not AI itself, so level D), 'Congress should clarify the responsibilities that AI developers and hosts have when a model goes rogue', and 'not histrionics and moratoriums'. The August and March remarks are X posts as quoted in news articles; the posts themselves were not opened. The 22 August post was also quoted identically by the Washington Examiner (https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/?p=4697477). The March post ('A moratorium is China First') was reported by Fox News on 26 March 2026; its exact post date (25 or 26 March) was not confirmed and it is not listed as a statement. The date 2026-08-10 for the pause remark comes from KUTV saying 'Monday' in an article dated Tuesday 11 August 2026. No source found showing he co-sponsored the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (S. 5493); the cosponsor list on congress.gov was not checked. Nothing found from him on superintelligence, extinction, or a China agreement. The Fetterman-Budd press release was seen only in search results and not opened.
